mainEntity.name: Which is cheaper, Google Forms or Microsoft Forms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither. Both form tools are free with a consumer account and bundled into the paid suites, and the suites are priced identically at every comparable tier: $7 a user a month annual and $8.40 monthly, then $14 and $16.80, then $22 and $26.40. Price cannot decide this comparison.

Yes, with any Google account, and Google publishes no response cap for it. What is documented is a limit of 300 pieces of content per form, which counts questions, descriptions, images, and videos together, plus 75 sections.

mainEntity.name: Does Google Forms have a 300 question limit?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and this is the most repeated myth about it. Google documents 300 pieces of content per form, which is not the same as 300 questions. Microsoft Forms is the product with a hard question cap, at 200 per form.

mainEntity.name: Can Google Forms be used for HIPAA data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with the right setup, contrary to what several AI answers currently claim. Google names Google Forms inside Drive in its HIPAA Included Functionality list, but an administrator has to review and accept a business associate agreement first, and PHI must not be used until they do.

mainEntity.name: Is Microsoft Forms covered by a BAA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Forms is named in Microsoft's commercial in-scope list, and the BAA is available by default through the Microsoft Online Services Data Protection Addendum for covered entities. Personal accounts are out of scope.

mainEntity.name: Does either one have AI form creation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Microsoft does, with a licence. Copilot in Forms requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, listed at $21 a user a month. Google's form drafting is part of Workspace Experiments, a trusted-tester programme, and it cannot build multi-section forms or edit an existing one.

TL;DR

Google Forms or Microsoft Forms: which should you choose?

Pick by the suite you already pay for, because Workspace and Microsoft 365 are priced identically at every comparable tier. Google Forms wins on free use, quiz analytics, and scale ceilings; Microsoft Forms wins on governance, AI assistance, and a BAA that is available by default. Both have shallow branching, which is where Formester comes in.

  1. Free use without a paid suiteGoogle Forms
  2. Quiz grading and analyticsGoogle Forms
  3. Governed data inside the tenantMicrosoft Forms
  4. Shipping AI assistance todayMicrosoft Forms
  5. Logic beyond forward-only branchingFormester
  6. Payments and an MCP serverFormester

When should you pick Formester?

  • The form needs real logic. Branch on any field and jump in any direction. Google branches at section level only, Microsoft branches forward only.
  • You need to take money. Stripe and PayPal fields on the free plan. Neither suite ships a payment field at any price.
  • You want AI drafting without an add-on. Prompt, question list, or PDF on the free plan. Copilot in Forms needs a licence listed at $21 a user, and Google's is trusted-tester only.

Stay in the suite when the responses must sit inside your tenant or under a BAA you already hold. Formester is GDPR, UK GDPR, and CCPA compliant, and is not HIPAA certified.

The honest read

Where does each one fall short?

Both are free with an account and good enough for a poll. These are the ceilings that send teams looking.

Neither branches properly

Google branches at section level and only from multiple choice or dropdown questions. Microsoft branches per question but forward only. Neither documents answer piping or compound rules.

Microsoft caps questions and degrades at scale

200 questions per form and 400 forms. Past 50,000 responses it falls back to CSV only, losing summary charts, individual response view, and manual grading.

Microsoft's free tier stops at 200 responses

On a personal account each form accepts 200 responses free, 1,000 on paid. Google Forms publishes no response cap on a consumer account.

Neither takes payments

No payment field in either product, so anything transactional needs a separate tool. Microsoft's own docs point users to Dynamics 365 Customer Voice once they outgrow Forms.

Migration

How do you move from either one to Formester?

Three steps, and the same process works whichever suite you are on.

1

Export your responses

In Google Forms, open Responses and link or download the Sheets file. In Microsoft Forms, open the Responses tab and choose Open results in Excel, then take a downloaded copy rather than the live-connected workbook.

Time: about five minutes per form.

2

Rebuild with AI

Paste your question list into Formester's AI generator or describe the form in a sentence. It drafts the questions, pages, and design in about half a minute, then you add the branching you could not build before.

Input options: plain prompt, pasted question list, or PDF upload.

3

Share the new link

Publish the Formester link or embed, send one test response, and keep the old form open for a week as a fallback before you close it.

Worth checking: Google Sheets permissions do not stay in sync with form permissions after creation.

Honest comparison

When should you stay on one of them?

Both are genuinely the right answer in some situations. Three of them.

It only needs to be free and quick

For a poll, an RSVP, or a class quiz, either is free and already in your account.

  • Google Forms is free with any Google account and publishes no response cap
  • Microsoft Forms is free with a personal account up to 200 responses per form
  • Formester's free plan is unlimited but carries our branding until Personal

Choose either suite for simple, internal, one-off forms

The data must stay in your tenant

Microsoft's live-connected Excel in OneDrive or SharePoint keeps responses under existing governance.

  • Responses land in the tenant with your existing access controls and retention
  • Forms is named in Microsoft's commercial in-scope list, with a BAA available by default via the DPA
  • External users cannot refresh the connected workbook, which is a real limitation

Choose Microsoft Forms when tenant governance is the requirement

You grade quizzes at scale

Google documents the richer grading analytics of the two.

  • Frequently missed questions, average, median, and range of scores
  • Graphs marked with correct answers and per-question grading
  • Microsoft's manual grading stops working past 50,000 responses

Choose Google Forms for quizzes and grading

Privacy and data ownership

Who owns your form data?

You do. Everything moving through your forms is Customer Data: the prompts you type, the structures the AI drafts, and every response someone submits. Section 4.4 of our Data Processing Addendum bars Formester from using any of it to train AI models, run advertising, or feed analytics and marketing. The Google Gemini integration that drafts forms works inside the same boundary.

Responses travel over TLS, sit encrypted at rest, and payment data carries an extra AES-256 layer through Stripe. Formester is GDPR, UK GDPR, and CCPA compliant. We are not SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA certified, and the security page says exactly that instead of hinting otherwise. Compensating controls are in place: encryption in transit and at rest, annual third-party penetration testing, enforced 2FA, and encrypted backups.

DPA §4.4 · January 2026
"Formester shall not use Customer Data for purposes of analytics, advertising, marketing, or training of artificial intelligence or machine learning models, except as strictly necessary to provide the Services."

Formester Data Processing Addendum, effective January 2026.
